analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: ASML tool demand; IFX good enough; VOD inline; TSMC Oct inline; BT delays Starlink; Auto1 appoints CFO
key_insights: US equities rebounded sharply overnight: S&P 500 +2.3%, Nasdaq 100 +3.4%, semis +6.8% despite Nvidia -4.3%, with more than 420 S&P names higher. Short covering and fresh tech buying drove the bounce after last week's sell-off.
Oil fell about 5% to $85 as Iran tensions eased. Trump said it is 'highly unlikely' he will order extensive strikes on Iran, conditional on Iran signing 'a very strong agreement'.
Asia is higher, with regional equities +1.8% and Korea +4%. GS describes this as catch-up with the earlier US and European rebound, not a fresh signal.

Positioning is light. GS PB shows US Info Tech net allocation at 14.4% of US net market value, in the 1st/1st/3rd percentiles on 1-year/3-year/5-year lookbacks. Semis positioning has almost fully round-tripped in 2026.
The market is hesitant to call an all-clear ahead of CPI on 11 Nov (GIR forecasts +16bps on core MoM) and CoreWeave/Nebius earnings later this week.

ASML: DigiTimes reports Samsung and SK Hynix are racing to secure ASML EUV tools for DRAM/HBM expansion amid expected supply shortfalls in 2027-28. SK Hynix disclosed an order of about KRW12tn, and both companies reportedly target KRW10-20tn. GS says this supports ASML's multi-year order visibility and pricing power but flags potential delays and higher equipment costs for memory capacity expansion.
ASML risk: investors asked whether the Nvidia CEO issue and a Democratic sweep could bring the Match Act back into focus, which would be a headwind for ASML and China sales.

SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility at Starbase, Texas, with initial investment of about $24 billion. GS calls it the cleanest positive in 24 hours because it monetizes existing offtake and sidesteps Texas grid politics.

The Senate advanced a bipartisan permitting bill 73-25, a procedural vote and not final passage, with the House the likelier hurdle. GS expects more conditions on data-centre development but not a nationwide moratorium, which it reads as pragmatic and favourable to infrastructure and well-capitalised developers.

The White House is considering new export controls on Nvidia's advanced AI chips, per The Information. Officials spoke with Congressional staff about controls that may form part of this year's National Defense Authorization Act.

European datacenter call with the EUDCA Secretary General: European data-centre development is unaffected by US mid-terms, the market could more than double by the early 2030s, and power grids are the single largest bottleneck. GS points to its European Power Basket (GSXEPOWR, 39 stocks).

Infineon (IFX) Q4 revenue was EUR4.71B, in line. EBIT was EUR1.12B vs consensus EUR1.10B, with margin 23.8% vs consensus 23.3%. FY27 guidance assumes EUR/USD 1.15 and revenue of about EUR20B vs consensus EUR19.8B.

IFX data-centre power supply revenue is guided to close to EUR4B, ahead of the sell side but at the bottom end of buy-side expectations of more than EUR4B. GS notes management has a reputation for conservative guidance. FY27 adjusted gross margin is guided mid-to-high 40% range, segment result margin mid 20% range, investments EUR3.0-3.5B and free cash flow about EUR1.8B.
TSMC October sales were NT$586bn, +14.7% MoM and +59.7% YoY, tracking at 34% of 4Q26 consensus, in line.

Vodafone H1 adjusted EBITDAaL was EUR6.45B, 0.9% light, with an FCF miss. FY27 guidance was raised to adjusted EBITDAaL of EUR13.2-13.4B (street EUR13.3B) and adjusted FCF of EUR2.8-3.0B (street EUR2.8B), which GS reads as about a 2% FCF upgrade driven by UK and Europe through cost cuts.

Vodafone Germany remains the bear debate: excluding 1&1 wholesale revenue and the ECJ provision, German EBITDA is still down about 4% y/y in H1. Vodafone Deutschland will cut 2,300 jobs, about 19% of the German workforce.
Sunrise Q3 was in line with the street and FY26 guidance was confirmed. Q3 revenue was CHF732m. Adjusted FCF was CHF32.5M vs CHF36.7M a year ago, a miss on working capital.

GIR (Jim Schneider) calls semis 'clearly oversold'. About 35GW of 2027 datacenter capacity is largely under construction, which GS says leaves near-term AI capex relatively insulated. GIR sees compelling risk/reward in NVDA, AVGO, AMAT, LRCX and memory.

GS trading desk: favour AVGO and NVDA, which at current valuations imply no growth past 2027. Favour AMAT and LRCX on the view that zero additional capex increases beyond 2027 is highly unlikely. Favour SK Hynix and Samsung, which trade below total tangible book.

Tesla and SpaceX's Terafab reportedly targets 1m wafers per month, including 700k DRAM and 300k logic by 2032, near Samsung's reported 650-700k wafers per month DRAM capacity. Terafab has reportedly reopened talks with TSMC and is considering Intel 14A for logic.
Onsemi has reportedly abandoned its planned US$2 billion silicon carbide expansion in Roznov, Czech Republic, per DigiTimes on 9 November 2026, linked to competition from cheaper Chinese wafers.

BT is delaying the launch of its Starlink satellite broadband partnership after service disruptions in Ukraine, per the Financial Times. The CEO later confirmed a launch 'in the coming months', versus an earlier target of 2H 2026.

Flows: asset managers were roughly flat, with demand in tech and financials vs supply in communication services. Hedge funds were net buyers, largely via macro products. Floor activity was 5 on a 1-10 scale.
Auto1 appoints Jörg Pietzner, currently at Deutsche Börse AG, as CFO effective 1 January 2027.

earnings_insights: Infineon Q4 (reported): revenue EUR4.71B in line, EBIT EUR1.12B vs consensus EUR1.10B, margin 23.8% vs consensus 23.3%, against guidance of about 23%.
Infineon FY27 guidance: revenue about EUR20B vs Infront consensus EUR19.8B (EUR/USD 1.15). GS says guided FY27 topline and segment result are 1% and 3% ahead of Vara consensus.
Infineon also raised humanoid/robot revenue content from 500k to 1,000 per robot.
Vodafone H1 (reported): adjusted EBITDAaL EUR6.45B, 0.9% light, with a 2.6% light and an FCF miss. Group service revenue was 1.8% ahead and Europe 1% ahead.
Vodafone FY27 guidance (new): adjusted EBITDAaL EUR13.2-13.4B vs street EUR13.3B, adjusted FCF EUR2.8-3.0B vs street EUR2.8B.
Sunrise Q3 (reported): revenue CHF732m, adjusted FCF CHF32.5M vs CHF36.7M a year ago. OFCF beat on lower capex, FCF missed on working capital, FY26 guidance confirmed.
TSMC October monthly sales (reported): NT$586bn, +14.7% MoM and +59.7% YoY, tracking at 34% of 4Q26 consensus.
